correctness.rationale: For fixed 0<ε<1, the odd analytic graph transform is a contraction on a small sup-norm ball and its linearized graph equation I−qC_(A^-1), q=(1−ε)/(1+ε), is invertible by a Neumann series. Thus the small graph is attracting, analytic and odd in μ; ergodicity gives the exponent in one iterate of the original map. Independently, project the integer frequency vectors onto the expanding eigendirection of A^-T: their nonzero projections are proportional to powers of λ=(3+√5)/2. After pair cancellations, a largest term can occur only once in a signed sum of at most four, and reaching it requires three positive lower powers. Three copies of the preceding power overshoot; two leave a residual strictly between the two preceding powers, since 1/λ<λ−2<1; at most one undershoots since 1/λ+2/λ²<1. This validates the all-index moment reduction, not just a finite scan. With κ=1−q², the derivative is q/(1−κ sin²(πx)); its cubic map coefficient is qκπ²/3 and its log-derivative coefficients are κπ² and π⁴(κ²/2−κ/3). The first graph response has second moment 1/(2κ) and fourth moment 3/(4κ²)−3/(8(1−q⁴)). Its cross moment with the cubic graph response is q²π²/3 times that fourth moment, by splitting off the first j kicks against the backward shift. Substitution gives π²/2 and π⁴(1+3q²)/(16κ), the latter exactly the frozen quartic coefficient. Analytic evenness controls the remainder for each fixed ε; no endpoint uniformity is assumed.
residual_risks: The finite diagnostic does not prove the all-index resonance assertion; the power comparison does. The expansion is local at fixed ε and does not control ε approaching 0 or 1.

value.rationale: The transverse exponent is a stability observable of an independently studied deterministic collision model. The exact curvature is a parameter-universal benchmark, whereas fourth order quantifies how contraction first changes that response without phase dependence. This provides analytic information beyond the unforced value and numerics without claiming a global basin or collision threshold.
